verbalization: Octadeca-6,9,12-trienoic acid is linked to NADH dehydrogenase [ubiquinone] 1 alpha subcomplex subunit 11 through a complex cascade of molecular interactions. The evidence suggests that this fatty acid acts as a target for the epigenetic regulators EZH2/SUZ12/EED/RBBP7/RBBP4, which are involved in chromatin modification and gene regulation. These regulators, in turn, are targeted by a specific metabolite that influences the activity of the NADH dehydrogenase complex. This implies that the fatty acid may modulate the function of the NADH dehydrogenase through its interaction with the epigenetic machinery, potentially affecting metabolic processes by altering gene expression. The relationship is supported by the direct targeting of the NADH dehydrogenase subunit by the epigenetic regulators, which suggests a role in cellular metabolism or signaling pathways.
